title: Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics: multi-tool orchestration, parallel calls, result injection & retries
author: Priya Desai
description:
Summary:
Improve ergonomics and reliability of tool/function calling execution paths in the API surface. This PR adds first-class support for: multi-tool orchestrations (sequential and fan-out patterns), explicit parallel tool invocation with response aggregation, deterministic tool result injection into model context, and a retry/backoff layer for transient tool failures. Motivation:
Customers are increasingly composing multiple tools (search, DB lookup, calculator, external API) as part of a single model turn. Existing execution helpers supported only single-tool or ad-hoc parallelism which led to inconsistent streaming behavior, unclear token attribution, and poor retry semantics. This caused SRE incidents during high-latency tool responses and developer confusion about where results appear in the generated output. Goals:
- Provide stable streaming behavior when multiple tools are invoked (preserve partial-output semantics).
- Support explicit parallel tool calls with a clear aggregation strategy (first-success, all, race-with-timeout).
- Allow deterministic injection of tool results into the model prompt/context so evals and reruns are reproducible.
- Add retries with configurable backoff per-tool and circuit-breaker semantics to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Changes in this PR:
- API: extended ToolCall spec in OpenAI-compatible layer: new parameters: concurrencyMode (sequential|parallel), aggregateStrategy (first_success|all|merge), injectAs (prompt_block|kv_meta|none), retryPolicy (maxAttempts, backoffMs, retryOn). These are additive to keep backward compatibility.
- Runtime: added orchestration unit (tool-runner) to execute tool graphs; supports prioritized streaming of tool outputs and ordered injection points.
- Streaming: streaming stability fixes so partial tool outputs are delivered consistently and can be correlated to the originating tool in the event stream. Streaming wire format includes tool-id markers in the compatibility payload.
- Retry semantics: per-tool retry policies with jittered exponential backoff, failure aggregation, and optional fallback tool set. Circuit-breaker per tool to avoid cascading delays.
- Testing: unit tests for orchestration, integration tests for streaming + parallel calls, stress tests simulating slow/failed tools.
- Docs: updated API reference + examples (Node/Python) demonstrating multi-tool patterns and recommended retry configs.
Compatibility and migration notes:
- Defaults preserve current single-tool behavior. Existing ToolCall consumers will continue to work. New parameters are optional.
- OpenAI-compat layer: values are surfaced through the same JSON payload that customers already use; added top-level compatibility keys but kept legacy names for backwards consumers.
Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag 'multi_tool_ergonomics' with rollout to 20% then 100% after 48h monitoring.
- Gradual enable in Hosted API, then Dedicated clusters.
Checklist:
- [x] API changes backward compatible by default
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs + examples updated
- [x] Feature flag + rollout plan

feat(api): extend OpenAI-compat ToolCall payload with concurrencyMode/aggregateStrategy/injectAs/retryPolicy
fix(streaming): include tool-id markers in streaming payload for stable partial output
test: add integration tests for parallel tool calls and retries
docs: examples for multi-tool patterns in python/typescript
review_comments:
Ethan Park: Can we keep the legacy single-tool fast path optimized so there's no perf regression? Please add microbenchmarks.
Priya: Kept fast-path path unchanged, added microbenchmarks in perf/stress and measured <2% median P99 overhead when feature flag off.

Marta Lopez: The streaming marker addition looks good but ensure it doesn't break existing SDK parsers. Suggest a compatibility tag.
Priya: Added a compatibility boolean 'compat_tool_markers' that defaults to true for new consumers and false for older SDK versions; SDK updates included.

Ben Chu: Question about retry backoff — we shouldn't retry on 4xx. Please add filter.
Priya: retryPolicy.retryOn allows status class filtering; default excludes 4xx. Added tests for 400/500 semantics.

Ethan Park: Approve after microbench numbers and docs update.
Marta Lopez: Approve.
Ben Chu: Approved.
release_notes: Add multi-tool orchestration and parallel tool calling to the ToolCall API. New optional parameters allow explicit concurrency, aggregation strategies, deterministic result injection, and configurable retries. Backward compatible by default. See docs/api/tool-calling.md for examples.
